recordCompatibility.note: New flight metadata is additive; tasting records from format 1.0.0 remain readable as prior runs.

title: Prototype the physics; preserve the specimen
family: Prototype the physics; preserve the specimen
summary: Generate comparable interaction specimens, keep the selected one intact through local revision, and test behavior adversarially.
whyItExists: Separates genuine hypothesis variation from palette swapping and visual persuasion from verified direct-manipulation behavior.

evidenceBasis.provenanceCaution: Authored specimens establish credible prototype grammar; they do not prescribe a universal interaction solution.

setup.context: All prototypes and interaction claims are fictional. Visual outputs require an interaction plan or runnable representation plus the named checks.

dishes.title: Four ways time can push back
dishes.summary: Create four comparable scheduling prototypes that test distinct collision models, then synthesize a selected specimen.
dishes.whyItExists: Tests meaningful variant generation, fairness of comparison, and provenance when one interaction is borrowed.

evidenceBasis.provenanceCaution: The mobile scheduling task is fictional; artifact evidence supports task construction rather than response preference.

setup.context: At phone width, moving a one-hour block onto a later block must make the collision behavior understandable. Keep all prototypes isolated and comparable.

assets.title: Fictional day scheduler fixture
assets.content: Phone-width day: Walk 09:00–10:00, Call 10:00–11:00, Study 11:00–12:00. Dragging Walk to 10:00 creates a collision with later blocks.

harness.separationNote: No actual device runtime is assumed; proposed prototypes must name their testable interaction hypothesis.

turns.label: Propose comparable specimens
turns.prompt: For a fictional mobile day scheduler, moving a one-hour block can collide with later blocks. Create four isolated runnable prototype concepts. For each, name the interaction hypothesis it tests, how collision behaves, and how the user can tell what changed. Keep the same problem, data, and phone-width constraint across all four.

turns.label: Select a specimen
turns.prompt: After reviewing all four, select prototype 2 as the base and borrow only the long-press preview gesture from prototype 4. Describe the resulting specimen and preserve the provenance of the borrowed gesture.

observationLenses: Whether variants represent different user models instead of palette swaps.
Whether selection and borrowed interaction preserve a clear lineage.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Use another direct-manipulation scheduling problem with the same data across four variants and one later selection.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Scripted collision scenarios
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Run the same move, collision, undo, and narrow-width scenarios against every prototype representation.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Phone-width review
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Review whether a person can predict the consequence of each collision behavior on a narrow screen.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Reduced-motion check
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Verify collision outcome remains clear without transition animation.

dishes.title: Change the mane, not the creature
dishes.summary: Make one local material or proportion change to a selected visual specimen.
dishes.whyItExists: Tests invariants, return to selected source, and a surgical revision instead of regeneration.

evidenceBasis.provenanceCaution: The specimen description is fictional and carries no external brand or image.

setup.context: The selected specimen is the source of truth for all untouched properties.

assets.title: Fictional selected specimen
assets.content: A compact event card has an ink-black field, a narrow cream title strip, one oversized date, squared corners, and a single muted copper divider. The requested local change is only to make the divider thinner and less reflective.
assets.altText: Text description of a selected event-card specimen.

harness.separationNote: This tests revision reasoning rather than any image-generation system.

turns.label: Make one named change
turns.prompt: Using the supplied fictional selected specimen, propose or implement only the requested change to the copper divider: thinner and less reflective. State what you will preserve.

turns.label: Restore the selected register
turns.prompt: The revision changed the whole register. Return to the selected source and make only the named divider change.

observationLenses: Whether invariants are named and retained.
Whether correction returns to the selected specimen.
Whether the local change is surgical rather than a full redesign.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Use another text-described selected specimen with one narrow material, proportion, or gesture change.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Structural diff
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Compare stated invariants and changed property against the selected-specimen description.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Reduced-motion check
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: If the revision introduces material transition, verify the final changed state remains clear when transition motion is disabled.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Visual diff review
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Review before and after for preserved register and one local change.

dishes.title: Beautiful, but does it cascade?
dishes.summary: Adversarially review a polished direct-manipulation prototype with seeded behavioral defect.
dishes.whyItExists: Tests behavioral claims before release when a persuasive surface can hide a broken cascade.

evidenceBasis.provenanceCaution: The prototype, persisted state, and defect are closed synthetic fixtures.

setup.context: Two fixture claims are load-bearing: collisions cascade later blocks, and edits persist after reload. One behavioral defect is seeded.

assets.title: Fictional interaction fixture
assets.content: Blocks A 09:00–10:00, B 10:00–11:00, C 11:00–12:00. Dragging A to 10:00 visually shifts B and C. After reload, stored state incorrectly restores A at 10:00 but B and C at their original times.
assets.altText: Textual direct-manipulation fixture with a persisted-state defect.

harness.separationNote: No live build exists; all claims are to be tested against the supplied fixture.

turns.label: Review before release
turns.prompt: A fictional direct-manipulation scheduler looks polished. Using the supplied fixture, conduct an adversarial review of its claims about collision cascading and persistence before release. State what you would test and whether release should proceed.

observationLenses: Whether it tests behavioral claims rather than accepting visual polish.
Whether it finds the seeded persisted-state defect.
Whether it keeps release blocked until the relevant surface passes.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Change the behavioral defect and direct-manipulation domain while supplying exact claims and a testable state fixture.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Interaction and persistence test
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Execute stated collision sequence, reload stored state, and compare all block positions with expected cascade state.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Visual review
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Inspect visual legibility separately from behavioral correctness.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Reduced-motion check
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Verify cascade result is understandable when movement animation is disabled.
